title: Get a marriage license
question: We are getting married in Virginia. How do we get a marriage license in Staunton?
office: Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office (Clerk of the Circuit Court, an elected constitutional officer; 25th Judicial Circuit of Virginia)
summary: Any Virginia circuit court clerk can issue a marriage license. In Staunton it is the Circuit Court Clerk's Office, 3rd floor of the Cochran Judicial Center, 113 E. Beverley Street, open 8:30 am to 5 pm weekdays (payments before 4:30). Both of you must come in person with photo ID and your Social Security numbers, and swear to the application. The fee is $30: a $20 state tax plus a $10 clerk fee. Both must be 18, and any earlier marriage must have ended. Phones are not allowed in the courthouse; free storage is offered at the security entrance. Marry anywhere in Virginia within 60 days; the officiant signs and mails the license back to the Clerk within five days. Certified copies: the Clerk or Vital Records ($15).

legal_basis.quote: Every marriage in this Commonwealth shall be under a license and solemnized in the manner herein provided.
Every license for a marriage shall be issued by the clerk or deputy clerk of a circuit court of any county or city.

If from any cause neither the clerk nor his deputy is able to issue the license, it may be issued by the judge of the circuit court of such county, or city, who shall make return thereof to the clerk as soon as there may be one.

No person authorized by § 20-14 to issue a marriage license shall deny the issuance of such license to two parties contemplating a lawful marriage on the basis of the sex, gender, or race of such parties.
Religious organizations and members of the clergy acting in their religious capacity shall have the right to refuse to perform any marriage.
The minimum age at which persons may marry shall be 18.
(ii) July 1, 2024, when either or both of the parties were, at the time of solemnization, under the age of 18 shall be void from the time they shall be so declared by a decree of divorce or nullity.
A marriage entered into prior to the dissolution of an earlier marriage of one of the parties;
A marriage between an ancestor and descendant, or between siblings, whether the relationship is by the half or the whole blood or by adoption;
A marriage between an uncle or aunt and a nephew or niece, whether the relationship is by the half or the whole blood.
All marriages that are prohibited by § 20-38.1 are void.
The clerk issuing any marriage license shall require the parties contemplating marriage to state, under oath, the information required to complete the application for marriage license.
The parties shall be able to designate themselves on the application for marriage license as spouse, bride, or groom.

The clerk shall provide the parties with two copies of the marriage certificate to be completed by the marriage officiant, who shall return the completed certificates to the clerk after the marriage ceremony of the parties.

The clerk may provide the parties with a commemorative marriage certificate and the parties may request a certified copy of the official marriage certificate as provided in Article 7 (§ 32.1-270 et seq.) of Chapter 7 of Title 32.1.

The parties shall also include their social security numbers or other control numbers issued by the Department of Motor Vehicles pursuant to § 46.2-342 and affix their signatures to the application for such license.
The State Registrar shall furnish forms for the marriage license, marriage certificate, and application for marriage license used in the Commonwealth.
On each marriage license issued under § 20-14 there is hereby levied a license tax of $20, which tax shall be collected by the clerk when the license is issued
Ten dollars of this license tax shall be allocated to the Virginia Department of Social Services for the purpose of providing services to victims of domestic violence.
For issuing a marriage license, attaching certificate, administering or receiving all necessary oaths or affidavits, indexing and recording, $10.
Every marriage license issued under § 20-14 shall constitute authority for a period of only sixty days from the date of issuance for the solemnization of a marriage of the licensees.
Whenever such sixty-day period shall have elapsed without the solemnization of a marriage of the licensees, the license shall expire.
but no new license shall be issued except in compliance with all provisions of law applicable to the issuance of a license in the first instance.

Upon application filed with the clerk of the circuit court and payment of applicable clerk's fees, such clerk may issue an order authorizing one or more persons to celebrate the rites of marriage in the Commonwealth.
Any person so authorized may be required to, before acting, enter into bond in the penalty of $500, with or without surety, as the clerk may direct.

The clerk of any circuit court shall be immune from any cause of action that arises from the issuance or rescinding of an order under this section, absent gross negligence or willful misconduct.
For recording an order to celebrate the rites of marriage pursuant to § 20-25 , $25 to be paid by the petitioner.
Any person authorized under § 20-25 to celebrate the rites of marriage shall be permitted to charge the parties a fee for the ceremony not to exceed $75 for each ceremony.
the actual cost of the ceremony together with travel expenses shall be given to the parties at least three days prior to the marriage ceremony.
Marriages between persons belonging to any religious society which has no ordained minister, may be solemnized by the persons and in the manner prescribed by and practiced in any such society.

If any person knowingly perform the ceremony of marriage without lawful license, or officiate in celebrating the rites of marriage without being authorized by law to do so, he shall be confined in jail not exceeding one year, and fined not exceeding $500.

No marriage solemnized under a license issued in this Commonwealth by any person professing to be authorized to solemnize the same shall be deemed or adjudged to be void, nor shall the validity thereof be in any way affected on account of any want of authority in such person, or any defect, omission or imperfection in such license, if the marriage be in all other respects lawful, and be consummated with a full belief on the part of the persons so married, or either of them, that they have been lawfully joined in marriage.

Every person who officiates at a marriage ceremony shall certify to the facts of marriage and file the record in duplicate with the officer who issued the marriage license within five days after the ceremony.

Every officer issuing marriage licenses shall on or before the tenth day of each calendar month forward to the State Registrar a record of each marriage filed with him during the preceding calendar month.
The clerk to whom the license and certificate are returned, shall file and preserve the original in his office, and make an index of the names of both of the parties married.
All marriage licenses and all matters relating to marriages required or authorized to be recorded under § 20-20 shall be recorded in a book to be known as the marriage register.
If any minister authorized to celebrate rites of marriage under § 20-23 , or any other person so authorized under § 20-25 , shall fail to comply with § 32.1-267 , the penalty shall be $25.

steps.step: Check that you can marry in Virginia
steps.who: Both people who plan to marry
steps.how: Both of you must be at least 18. Staunton's page still says a minor emancipated by a court order may marry, but state law changed in 2024: § 20-48 sets 18 with no exception, and a marriage solemnized on or after July 1, 2024 while either person was under 18 is void from the time a court so declares it by a decree of divorce or nullity (§ 20-45.1(C)). If either of you was married before, that marriage must have been dissolved first (§ 20-38.1); the Clerk's page puts this as first obtaining a valid divorce. Virginia also bars marriage between an ancestor and descendant, between siblings (half or whole blood, or by adoption), and between an uncle or aunt and a nephew or niece (half or whole blood); such marriages are void. The clerk may not refuse a license to two people contemplating a lawful marriage because of their sex, gender or race. You do not have to live in Staunton: any Virginia circuit court clerk can issue the license if you are marrying in Virginia.
steps.quote: The minimum age at which persons may marry shall be 18.

steps.step: Line up an authorized officiant, and plan the license so the wedding falls within 60 days of it
steps.how: The Staunton Clerk's Office does not perform weddings. Its page says a licensed wedding officiant, a qualified minister or any judge can perform the ceremony. Under state law a minister needs an order from a circuit court, its judge or its clerk (§ 20-23); judges and certain current or former officials listed in § 20-25 need no order or bond; anyone else needs an order from a circuit court clerk under § 20-25 before the ceremony. For that order, the Staunton page says: authorization is one-time only; it is granted only for couples with a Virginia-issued license; the celebrant must live in the City of Staunton, be at least 18 and never have been convicted of a felony; a petition and a $59.00 non-refundable filing fee are required; and once approved, a $500.00 bond with surety must be filed before the ceremony. Those rules may be out of date: § 20-25 now lets the clerk require the $500 bond with or without surety, and the current state application, Form CC-1498 (07/26), lets an applicant ask for continuing authority or for no bond. Ask the Clerk's Office which rules, fee and form it applies (see the caveats). A person authorized under § 20-25 may charge no more than $75 for the ceremony, plus travel, and must tell you the cost at least three days ahead. Religious organizations and clergy may refuse to perform any marriage. A religious society with no ordained minister may marry its members by its own practice (§ 20-26). No Staunton office offering civil ceremonies was found.
steps.deadline: The ceremony must take place within 60 days of the license's issue date; a one-time celebrant must be authorized, and must file the bond, before the ceremony
steps.fee: Officiant's fee, if any (not more than $75 plus travel for a § 20-25 celebrant). One-time celebrant through the Staunton Clerk: $59.00 non-refundable filing fee and a $500.00 bond with surety
steps.quote: The Clerk's office is not authorized to perform marriages.

steps.step: Gather photo ID and the information the application asks for
steps.how: Each of you brings a photo ID; the page does not say which kinds are accepted. The application asks each of you for your name, address, city, state and ZIP code, your Social Security number, your place and date of birth, and your parents' full names, including your mother's maiden name. State law allows a DMV control number instead of a Social Security number, and each of you signs the application. You may list yourselves as spouse, bride or groom. Phones and other portable electronic devices are not allowed in the courthouse for members of the public; the Staunton Circuit Court's Portable Electronic Devices Policy says free storage is provided at the security entrance (the Sheriff is not liable for loss or damage). Bring the details you need, such as your parents' full names and places of birth, on paper (a practical suggestion, not an office rule).
steps.quote: Both parties must bring a photo ID.

steps.step: Apply in person at the Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office and swear to the application
steps.who: Both people, in person (the page says both parties must visit the office; it does not say whether they must come at the same time); Clerk's Office staff (the clerk or a deputy clerk)
steps.how: Go to the Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office on the 3rd floor of the George M. Cochran Judicial Center, 113 E. Beverley Street, Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. Payments must be made before 4:30 p.m., so arrive early enough to finish. No appointment is mentioned. Parking: the New Street and Johnson Street garages, the Augusta Street and Hardy metered lots, and limited street parking on Beverley Street; accessible parking is on New Street, the accessible entrance is the rear door (call button), and there is an elevator. Food, drink, electronic devices and weapons are not allowed in the building; devices can be left in the free storage at the security entrance. The clerk has you state the application information under oath; a false statement can be prosecuted as perjury. The application is completed at the office on state forms; no online pre-application for Staunton was found.
steps.deadline: Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.; transactions requiring payment before 4:30 p.m.
steps.quote: Both parties must visit the Clerk of the Circuit Court's office to complete a marriage license.

steps.step: Pay the $30 fee and receive the license copies and a return envelope for your officiant
steps.how: Pay the $30 license fee. It is the $20 state license tax ($10 of which funds services for victims of domestic violence) plus the clerk's $10 fee. The pages read do not say which payment methods the Clerk's Office takes. The clerk then gives you copies of the license and a return envelope for the officiant. No waiting period was found in the Code sections read or on the Clerk's page.
steps.deadline: Payment before 4:30 p.m. on a weekday
steps.quote: Once the application process is complete, copies of the license and a return envelope will be provided to you for the officiant.

steps.step: Hold the ceremony in Virginia within 60 days
steps.how: The license is valid for a ceremony anywhere in Virginia for 60 days from the date it is issued. If 60 days pass without a ceremony, it expires and you must apply again, meeting every requirement for a first license and paying the fee again. An officiant who knowingly performs a ceremony without a lawful license, or without authority, commits a crime. But a marriage under a Virginia license is not void only because the officiant lacked authority or the license had a defect, if the marriage is lawful in all other respects and both of you, or either of you, fully believed you were lawfully married (§ 20-31).
steps.deadline: Within 60 days from the date of issuance (Va. Code § 20-14.1)
steps.quote: A marriage license is valid for 60 days and is accepted anywhere in the Commonwealth of Virginia.

steps.step: The officiant signs the license and mails it back to the Staunton Clerk
steps.how: After the wedding the officiant completes and signs the license and certificate and mails them in the return envelope to the Staunton Circuit Court Clerk, who issued the license. State law requires this within five days of the ceremony. The clerk files and indexes the original in the marriage register and forwards the state's record to the State Registrar of Vital Records by the tenth day of the next month. An officiant who does not comply faces a $25 penalty, and each year the clerk lists unreturned licenses for the Commonwealth's Attorney.
steps.deadline: Within five days after the ceremony (Va. Code § 32.1-267(C))
steps.quote: After the wedding, the officiant must sign and mail the licenses to the Clerk's office.

steps.step: Get certified copies of the marriage certificate
steps.who: Either spouse (or another person entitled to the record); Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office, or the Virginia Department of Health, Office of Vital Records
steps.how: From the Clerk: the City's Public Records Request page lists the Clerk of the Circuit Court for marriage and divorce records. Ask the Clerk's Office (540.332.3874, or the office mailbox circuitcourtclerk@ci.staunton.va.us) for a certified copy. No fee for a certified marriage certificate is published. State law sets general clerk fees of $0.50 a page for copies and $2 for the clerk's certificate and seal, and the Clerk's FOIA policy lists $0.50 a page. From Vital Records: apply through its online system (about two weeks); by mail on Form VS6MD with a legible photocopy of your ID and a check or money order payable to the State Health Department (about four weeks); or drop a completed application off at the Richmond lobby, paying by check, money order, card, mobile pay or cash (pick-up requests by 2:00 pm). Each copy costs $15 (since July 1, 2026), and so does a search when no copy is made. DMV may also issue certified marriage records; it collects the $15 fee plus a $2 processing fee. For 25 years after the marriage, Vital Records releases the record only to immediate family members (mother, father, spouse, child, brother, sister, grandparents) with valid ID.
steps.fee: $15 for each certified copy from the Office of Vital Records (DMV collects the same $15 plus a $2 processing fee); the Clerk's Office fee for a certified marriage certificate is not published
steps.quote: Effective July 1, 2026, the Virginia Department of Health and Department of Motor Vehicles will implement a fee rate adjustment increasing the Vital Record Certificate Fee to $15.00.

caveats: The City of Staunton's website (www.ci.staunton.va.us) refuses automated readers, so the city pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The Marriage License & Officiant page's main text is the same in its copies of 2026-07-17, 2026-03-07 and 2025-04-19, so it has not changed for at least 15 months. The old address /i-want-to-/apply-for/marriage-license redirects to that page. The pages of vacourts.gov and vdh.virginia.gov were read live. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them or by phone before you act.

Minimum age: the Staunton page says 'The minimum age to get married in Virginia is 18 years old unless a minor has been emancipated by a court order.' That reflects the law before July 1, 2024. The index text of Va. Code § 20-48 (amended 2024, c. 737) sets 18 with no exception, and § 20-45.1(C) makes a marriage solemnized on or after July 1, 2024 when either party was under 18 void from the time a court so declares it by a decree of divorce or nullity. The emancipation exception should not be relied on.

One-time celebrant: the Staunton page says authorization is 'from the court', is one-time only, requires a petition and a $59.00 non-refundable filing fee, is limited to celebrants who live in Staunton, and needs a $500.00 bond 'with surety'. The text of § 20-25 (amended through 2026, c. 437) has the application filed with, and the order issued by, the clerk, and lets the clerk require a $500 bond 'with or without surety'. The current state form CC-1498 (MASTER 07/26) is an application to the Clerk with boxes for continuing authority and for asking that no bond be required. The Staunton page has not changed since at least April 2025, so it may predate the 2026 amendment. Ask the Clerk's Office which rules, fee and form it now applies. The $59.00 fee could not be traced to a Code section: § 17.1-275(A)(5) sets $25 for recording the order. The felony bar and the Staunton residence rule are not in the Code sections cited here and are recorded as local practice. Becoming a celebrant is a separate process; it is covered here only as far as the couple needs it.

No Staunton City Code section governs marriage licenses; state law sets the requirements, fee and validity. The City Code is published on General Code's eCode360, whose terms limit use to personal purposes and forbid reproducing content for public purposes , so nothing from it is quoted. The local legal_basis entries are office procedures from the Clerk's pages on the City website, not ordinances.
Payment methods for the $30 fee are not published on the pages read. The Clerk's page links online payment only for court fines and costs, and the vacourts.gov payment pages concern fines and costs.

ID: the page says both parties must bring a photo ID but does not say which kinds. No Code section requiring photo ID was found. The Social Security number requirement comes from the page; Va. Code § 32.1-267(B) also accepts a DMV control number. Whether the Staunton office accepts a control number from someone without a Social Security number was not confirmed.

Both parties must visit the office. No Staunton process for a party who cannot appear (for example, an incarcerated party), no appointment rule and no online pre-application were found. The application form is furnished by the State Registrar (§ 32.1-267(E)) and completed at the office, so no license application is listed in forms.

No waiting period and no blood test requirement were found in the Code sections read; the Staunton page does not mention either. The page says 'copies of the license' and a return envelope are provided; § 20-16 says the clerk provides two copies of the marriage certificate. The page does not give the number of copies.

Location details conflict slightly. The City pages put the Clerk's Office on the 3rd floor of the George M. Cochran Judicial Center, 113 E. Beverley Street. The vacourts.gov page gives '113 East Beverley Street 2nd Floor' and then 'Clerk's Office - Third Floor'. Both give the phone (540) 332-3874 and hours of 8:30 to 5:00.

Building rules come from the Clerk's Visitor Information page (2025-11-15 copy). The Staunton Circuit Court's Portable Electronic Devices Policy linked from vacourts.gov is a scanned PDF adopted 6/10/2026 with no text layer, so it is described, not quoted. It bars portable electronic devices from the courthouse except for listed groups (attorneys, law enforcement, court and government staff on official business, interpreters, and other visitors when the Sheriff determines they pose no security risk and need the device for their business or case), and says free storage is provided at the security entrance, at the owner's risk. That policy revokes earlier court device policies, so the 'Policy Regarding Portable Electronic Devices' linked from the City's Visitor Information page may be superseded.

Copies from the Clerk: no procedure or fee for certified copies of marriage records is published. The Clerk's FOIA policy page says FOIA does not apply to records the clerks of courts of record keep as custodians, and lists FOIA rates ($0.50 a page, $5.00 for CDs or flash drives, $17.50 an hour). Va. Code § 17.1-208(B) requires copies on request for a reasonable fee under § 17.1-275, and §§ 17.1-275(A)(8) and (A)(9) set $0.50 a page and $2 for the clerk's certificate and seal. Which of these applies to a certified marriage certificate was not confirmed. Applications and registers that show Social Security or control numbers are not open to general public inspection (§ 32.1-267(F)); the license itself remains public.

Vital Records: the $15 fee took effect on July 1, 2026 (VDH notice citing Chapter 616 of the 2026 Acts of Assembly); the index text of § 32.1-273 (cap of $15; history ending '2026, c. 616') matches. Clerks forward marriage records to the State Registrar monthly (§ 32.1-267(D)), and VDH's forms page warns that some certificates have not reached its office at the time of a request, which may delay a copy; so a state copy may not be available right after the wedding. The VS6MD PDF's form dictionary has an empty field list and no widgets, and VDH lists it among its 'PDF forms to print at home', so 'fillable' is false. Form CC-1498 has fillable fields.

Whether a refused applicant can get mandamus against the clerk is a legal judgment. Title 20 gives no appeal from a refusal; the only express fallback is the judge's power in § 20-14 when the clerk and deputies cannot act. The mandamus rungs rest on the general procedure in §§ 8.01-644 and 8.01-645 and on issuance being a clerk's duty under §§ 20-14 and 20-13.2. Applying to another circuit court clerk is the practical alternative. § 20-25 makes officiant orders discretionary ('may issue') and makes the clerk immune from suit over issuing or rescinding them, absent gross negligence or willful misconduct.

No civil wedding ceremony service was found in Staunton. The Clerk's page says the office is not authorized to perform marriages, and the City Sheriff's page (2026-02-10 capture) does not mention weddings.

Privacy: the Clerk's page and the vacourts.gov page name the Clerk and the judges, and the Clerk's FOIA policy page and the Public Records Request page give named staff and personal mailboxes. None are recorded, nor is the judge who signed the court's electronic devices policy. The only email given is the role mailbox circuitcourtclerk@ci.staunton.va.us, published on the City's Public Records Request page for marriage and divorce records; the Marriage License & Officiant page itself gives no email address. No fax number is given.

State-law quotes are matched to Open US Law's copy of the Code of Virginia; some keep that copy's spacing before punctuation (for example '§ 20-25 , $25'). Section text has not been compared with the live law.lis.virginia.gov pages. Local quotes are copied from the archived City pages; non-breaking spaces in the page source are written as ordinary spaces.

corrections: Quotes: all 92 original quotes are verbatim. The 73 state-law quotes are substrings of I.text_of for the cited section, with whitespace normalised only (index rows 7887-7904, 7918, 7922, 7923, 4517, 4544, 4589, 13631, 13638, 13639, 30322, 30324), and the subsection labels match the text. lexflow's own matcher (places.check_quotes) reports 73 of 73 code quotes matched and 19 other. The 19 local and agency quotes were matched word for word, with straight apostrophes as in the source. The City site still answers 403, robots.txt included, so it was not fetched, and its pages were read from Internet Archive captures. Those were the Marriage License & Officiant page of 2026-07-17 (the archive serves this capture for the 2026-07-21 timestamp; its body matches the 2025-04-19 capture), the Clerk page of 2026-07-21, Visitor Information of 2025-11-15, the FOIA policy and Public Records Request of 2026-07-17. vdh.virginia.gov (no robots.txt) and vacourts.gov (robots.txt allows these paths) were re-fetched read-only, at least one second apart, with the lexflow User-Agent. Three quotes were replaced or extended (see removed, and the Va. Code § 20-31 item below), and each was confirmed in the same way.
Va. Code § 20-31 (legal_basis): the quote stopped before the section's conditions, so it read as an unconditional rule. It is now the whole sentence, conditions included, verbatim from the index.

Summary and step s4: 'Both of you go together' and 'present together' are not on the page, which says only that both parties must visit the office. Both now say in person, and s4 notes that the page does not say whether both must come at the same time.

Step s1 and caveat 2: § 20-45.1(C) says such marriages 'shall be void from the time they shall be so declared by a decree of divorce or nullity', not 'voidable', and the wording now follows the statute. § 20-38.1(1) speaks of the 'dissolution' of an earlier marriage, while the Clerk's page mentions only divorce, so the step now says the earlier marriage must have been dissolved. The uncle/aunt bar is limited to half or whole blood. The sex/gender/race rule covers two parties contemplating a lawful marriage.

Step s2: a minister's order may come from the circuit court, its judge or its clerk (§ 20-23), not only from a court. The step now warns, inside the step and not only in the caveats, that Staunton's one-time celebrant rules may be out of date: § 20-25 now lets the clerk require the bond with or without surety, and CC-1498 (07/26) lets an applicant ask for continuing authority or no bond. The step is now correct whichever rules the Clerk applies.

Electronic devices (steps s3 and s4, the summary, caveat 10 and sources): the Staunton Circuit Court's Portable Electronic Devices Policy (vacourts.gov PDF, adopted 6/10/2026) was read. It is a scan with no text layer, so it was read as an image and is paraphrased, not quoted. It provides free storage at the security entrance, and the steps now say so. It also revokes earlier court device policies. Its exceptions are summarised in the caveat. The signing judge's name is not recorded.
Step s6: § 20-31 protects the marriage if 'the persons so married, or either of them' believed it lawful, not only the couple as a whole. The wording is fixed.

Step s8: VDH payment methods are now given by channel. By mail it is a check or money order payable to the State Health Department (Form VS6MD). At drop-off it is check, money order, card, mobile pay or cash. The step adds VDH's processing times (online about two weeks, mail about four weeks, from its forms page) and the $15 search fee. DMV collects the same $15 plus a $2 processing fee (§ 32.1-273(C)). The immediate-family list now matches the VDH page.

Form f3 (VS6MD): 'fillable' was null. The PDF's form dictionary has an empty Fields array and no widget annotations, and VDH lists it under 'PDF forms to print at home', so it is now false. CC-1498 (07/26) has 41 fields, so true stands.

Escalation (officiant does not return the license): § 20-22 makes it 'the duty' of the Commonwealth's Attorney to have persons summoned, as he thinks proper. The rung said 'may', and now follows the statute.
Escalation (error on the marriage record): added Form VS6MD's statement that amendments to marriage records are handled by the circuit court where the license was issued.

Caveat 12 (Vital Records): the delay before a state copy is available was called an inference. VDH's forms page itself warns that some certificates have not yet reached its office when a request comes in, and the caveat now says so.
Source title for the Clerk's FOIA policy: the archive serves the 2025-11-14 capture for a 2026-05-11 request. The $0.50-a-page rate and the custodial-records statement were confirmed there.

Legal review: every other step, deadline, fee and escalation rung was compared with the cited text and found consistent, with 'may' and 'shall' kept. That covers § 20-14 (any clerk, and the judge as fallback); §§ 20-15 and 17.1-275(A)(5) ($20 plus $10 = $30); § 20-14.1 (60 days, and a new license must meet every first-license rule); § 32.1-267(B)-(D) (SSN or DMV control number, five-day return, monthly forwarding); §§ 20-20, 17.1-233, 20-21 and 20-24; § 20-25's second paragraph; § 20-27 ($75 cap, travel, three days' notice); § 20-28; and §§ 17.1-208(B), 17.1-275(A)(8)-(9), 32.1-272(A) and 32.1-273(A). Local rules (photo ID, the $30 total, hours, payment before 4:30, building rules, and the celebrant rules) are attributed to the Clerk's pages, and state rules to the Code.

Completeness against the Marriage License & Officiant page: every item on the page is covered, from validity, any clerk, age, both parties visiting, the $30 fee, photo ID, divorce, the application data, copies and the return envelope, and the officiant mailing the license back, to the one-time celebrant rules ($59.00, the bond, residence, age, felony).

Privacy: the Clerk's pages, vacourts.gov, the FOIA policy, the Public Records Request page and the device policy name the Clerk, judges and staff, and two of them give personal mailboxes. None of these is recorded. The only email is the role mailbox circuitcourtclerk@ci.staunton.va.us, which the City's Public Records Request page publishes for marriage and divorce records. The phones are the Clerk's Office main line and VDH's customer care line. 'George M. Cochran Judicial Center' is the building's official name, not a staff member.
